Let \(x=BC\). Put the origin at the circumcenter \(O\), and let the position vectors of \(A,B,C\) be \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b,\mathbf c\). Since \(O\) is the circumcenter,

\[
|\mathbf a|=|\mathbf b|=|\mathbf c|=R.
\]

The centroid is

\[
\mathbf g=\frac{\mathbf a+\mathbf b+\mathbf c}{3}.
\]

Let \(\mathbf h\) be the orthocenter of \(\triangle AGO\).

Because \(OG\) is along \(\mathbf g\) and \(AO\) is along \(\mathbf a\), the altitude conditions give

\[
(\mathbf h-\mathbf a)\cdot \mathbf g=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
(\mathbf h-\mathbf g)\cdot \mathbf a=0.
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbf h\cdot \mathbf g=\mathbf a\cdot \mathbf g,
\qquad
\mathbf h\cdot \mathbf a=\mathbf g\cdot \mathbf a.
\]

Since \(\mathbf b+\mathbf c=3\mathbf g-\mathbf a\),

\[
\mathbf h\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)
=3\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf g-\mathbf h\cdot\mathbf a
=2\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g. \tag{1}
\]

Now \(\mathbf h\) lies on line \(BC\), so \(\mathbf h=(1-t)\mathbf b+t\mathbf c\). Hence

\[
\mathbf h\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)=R^2+\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c. \tag{2}
\]

Also,

\[
x^2=|\mathbf b-\mathbf c|^2=2R^2-2\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c,
\]

so

\[
\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c=R^2-\frac{x^2}{2}.
\]

Therefore (2) becomes

\[
\mathbf h\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)=2R^2-\frac{x^2}{2}. \tag{3}
\]

Next compute \(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g\):

\[
\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g
=\frac13\left(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf a+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b+\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c\right).
\]

Using \(AB=11\) and \(AC=13\),

\[
\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b=R^2-\frac{121}{2},
\qquad
\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf c=R^2-\frac{169}{2}.
\]

Thus

\[
\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf g
=\frac13\left(3R^2-\frac{290}{2}\right)
=R^2-\frac{145}{3}.
\]

So from (1),

\[
\mathbf h\cdot(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)=2R^2-\frac{290}{3}. \tag{4}
\]

Equating (3) and (4),

\[
2R^2-\frac{x^2}{2}=2R^2-\frac{290}{3}.
\]

Hence

\[
\frac{x^2}{2}=\frac{290}{3}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
x^2=\frac{580}{3}.
\]

Therefore

\[
BC=x=\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}=\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{2\sqrt{435}}{3}}
\]
